The assigned guidance establishes a useful negative anchor: the seed’s fast target-blind oscillator saturates both velocity and acceleration, produces extreme moment load, and exits downward. I’m now comparing that failure against the quieter finite examples visually and numerically to identify which missing feedback capability is actually supported.

The visual comparison is decisive: all three “gentler” successors remain near the initial heading but are swept out through the right boundary in roughly 16.3–16.7 units, with only about 0.016–0.023 units of x-motion relative to local flow. The inherited turn-rate variant is the opposite failure mode—instability after 1.0 unit with million-scale RMS moment. The next candidate therefore needs rapid, bounded gait startup first; extra steering channels are not yet justified.

The skill’s visual-first procedure has now changed the policy direction: the evidence supports neither another low-frequency steering variant nor raw yaw-rate damping. I’m recording a single bounded “middle-envelope” hypothesis—fast energy-regulated startup, modest bearing-only curvature, and no extra wake/force channel—before editing the candidate, as required.

The candidate and both required evidence files are updated. The durable guidance now records two negative boundaries supported by prior rollouts: low saturation can simply mean passive downstream escape, and unscaled raw heading-rate coupling can destabilize before navigation begins.
